title: Lord of the sabbath (Mark 2:23–28)
hookLine: the disciples pick grain on the sabbath, and Jesus defends them

cards: A Saturday in Galilee. The grain is high on both sides of a footpath. Jesus and his friends are hungry, so as they walk, the disciples pull off a few heads of grain, rub them in their hands and eat.
Anyone could; the law of Moses let a passerby pick by hand from a neighbor's field. The trouble is the day.
It's the sabbath, the day of rest, and to some Pharisees watching, picking grain looks like harvesting, and harvesting is work. Why, they ask, are your disciples doing what isn't allowed?

teach.h: ONE DAY IN SEVEN, FOR EVERYONE.
teach.b: First, how much the sabbath mattered, and still matters. It's one of the Ten Commandments: one day in seven, no work, for everyone, including servants, foreigners and animals.
For Jews it was, and is, a gift and a sign of belonging to God, kept with real joy. So the Pharisees' question is serious, not petty; what counts as work is exactly what careful people argued about.
Remember David, he says, when he and his men were hungry, and the priest gave them the holy bread from the house of God, bread only priests were meant to eat. Need came first.

teach.h: THE SABBATH WAS MADE FOR MAN.
teach.b: Then the line, in the King James Bible: "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath." And one more sentence, the one that gives today its title: "Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath."

In the gospels, Son of Man is how Jesus often speaks of himself. So this isn't only a ruling about grain; Christian readers hear him claiming the right to say what the day of rest is for. A neighbor shares the first half.
Jewish teachers also taught that saving a life outweighs the sabbath, and one early rabbinic teaching says something very close: the sabbath is given to you, not you to the sabbath.

Many churches keep Sunday, the day of the resurrection, as their day of rest and worship. Some, like Seventh-day Adventists, keep Saturday. Either way the question stays the same: is my rest healing me?

how: Christians in many churches keep Sunday as a day of worship and rest in honor of the resurrection, while some churches, such as Seventh-day Adventists, keep the seventh day, Saturday, as the sabbath.

turn back and walk home first.
games.why: the disciples pick and eat, and when they're challenged, Jesus defends them: the sabbath was made for man.

practice: Ask your body what kind of tired it is: sleepy tired, needing a nap; people tired, needing quiet; screen tired, needing a window and some sky; worried tired, needing to put something down.
Don't solve it, just name it, and choose one small rest that fits that tiredness, for later today. If you pray, rest these minutes in God's company; if you don't, rest them anyway.
